text: Zalerol is a strong inhibitor of HTX-1A.
Zalerol is taken with food to reduce nausea.
Zalerol is approved for use in adults only.
Zalerol is stored below 25 degrees Celsius.
Zalerol is 92% bound to plasma proteins.
Kessustat is cleared almost entirely by HTX-6K.
Kessustat is dosed by body weight in patients under 50 kg.
Kessustat is contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment.
Kessustat is available as a generic formulation.
Kessustat has no known effect on the QT interval.

Zalerol's only described pharmacokinetic activity is strong inhibition of HTX-1A. Kessustat, however, is cleared almost entirely by HTX-6K — a different enzyme — and nothing in the provided data indicates Zalerol affects HTX-6K, Kessustat's absorption, or its distribution. Zalerol's 92% plasma protein binding raises a theoretical displacement concern, but Kessustat's protein binding is not provided, so no displacement-based interaction can be established. With no shared enzyme or mechanism between the two drugs, no clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction is expected on the information available.

MECHANISM: Zalerol inhibits HTX-1A; Kessustat is cleared by HTX-6K — no overlapping pathway, no inhibition of Kessustat's clearance
